name: Muscular Atrophy-Ataxia-Retinopathy-Diabetes Mellitus Syndrome
aliases: Muscular Atrophy with Ataxia, Retinitis Pigmentosa, and Diabetes Mellitus

criteria.description: Progressive muscular atrophy with distal and proximal muscle weakness
Cerebellar ataxia manifesting as gait and limb coordination impairment
Retinitis pigmentosa confirmed by ophthalmological examination and visual field testing
Non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus diagnosed by standard glucose tolerance tests
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all four major features: muscular atrophy, cerebellar ataxia, retinitis pigmentosa, and diabetes mellitus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not definitive due to limited data.

laboratory: Elevated fasting blood glucose consistent with diabetes mellitus
Normal or mildly elevated liver enzymes
imaging: Electromyography demonstrating chronic denervation and reinnervation
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance pattern
other: Ophthalmologic fundoscopy revealing bone spicule pigmentation characteristic of retinitis pigmentosa
Visual field testing showing peripheral constriction

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of diabetes mellitus in early stages

redFlags: Rapid progression of muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Sudden onset of visual loss or acute retinal detachment
references: Orphanet: Muscular atrophy-ataxia-retinitis pigmentosa-diabetes mellitus syndrome, ORPHA:2579
Recent case reports and reviews on MARD syndrome clinical features
